# [diagnostics] EVAP system faults

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

Remove the evaporative canister and blast compressed air into its vent valve. [t295]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Remove the evaporative canister from the vehicle.
2. Use an air compressor to blast compressed air into the vent valve located on the canister.

_Procedure reported by [t295]._

## Tools

- Air compressor [t295]

## Tips & gotchas

- [Partial] Expect a significant amount of dirt and debris (described as 'sand storm') to be expelled from the valve. [t295]
- Note that this issue is common enough that owners often wait for warmer weather before tackling it. [t295]

## Common mistakes

- Failing to properly clip electrical plugs back in after reassembly, which can cause intermittent codes. [t295]
